about: The hand review of every claim that passed check.mjs. A verdict and a reason for each, keyed by the claim's key in checked.json. A kept claim can have how it was filed corrected (kind, place, year, year_precision, who) and its confidence lowered, but the quote is never touched. Reviewed on 12 Nov 2026 (the pilot first, then the scale-up to every named garment, accessory, fabric, pattern and shoe) by reading each quote against the rules in prompt.md, and the article around it where the quote was unclear.

beatle-boots:origin:1.reason: London and 1961 are both in the quote. Medium because the same sentence also says the boots originated in 1958, with no place.

beatniks:origin:1.reason: Dates the name Beat Generation in New York, which is the scene rather than the look.

boat-shoes:origin:1.reason: Invented, year, person and town all in one sentence.

button-down-shirt:origin:1.reason: The sentence sits under the article's button-down collar entry, so it is about this collar. Medium because the quote needs that context.

buzz-cut:origin:1.reason: Serbia is the nationality of the man who invented hair clippers, not where the haircut started.

crew-cut:origin:1.reason: Harvard, Yale, Princeton and Cornell are unmistakably the United States. It is where the name comes from, and the quote hedges.

denim-jacket:origin:1.reason: First recorded in the United States, with year and maker.

denim-jacket:rival:1.reason: Says which collection holds the jacket, not where it was made.

goth:origin:1.reason: Emerged in the United Kingdom in the early 1980s.

greasers:origin:1.reason: Emerged in the United States (and Canada) in the 1950s.

harrington-jacket:origin:1.reason: A British company's claim, hedged in the quote.

harrington-jacket:rival:1.reason: The article sets Grenfell's claim against Baracuta's.

hip-hop:origin:1.reason: American cities are named. No date.

houndstooth:origin:1.reason: Hedged in the quote (may have originated).

jeans:origin:1.reason: A US patent, with the year and both names.

jeans:root:1.reason: The jean fabric is traced to Genoa in the 16th century.

jeans:root:2.reason: Denim is traced to weavers in Nîmes copying jean.

levis-501:origin:1.reason: About the rivet patent, not the 501. The article is about the whole company and the same fact is already filed under jeans.

loafers:origin:1.reason: One of the first designs, in London. No date.

loafers:rival:1.reason: A second first design, in Norway, with a year.

miniskirt:origin:1.reason: The article's main account, and it names the dispute itself.

miniskirt:rival:1.reason: Courrèges is credited in the same sentence as Quant.

miniskirt:rival:2.reason: A named journalist's competing claim for a British designer.

miniskirt:rival:3.reason: The article calls it an alternative origin story.

platform-boots:root:1.reason: The article names Venetian zoccoli as the predecessor of platform shoes.

polo-shirt:origin:1.reason: Where Lacoste first wore his shirt, which is not quite where it was made.

polo-shirt:rival:1.reason: The article does not set this against Lacoste. It says where polo players wore the shirt first, so it is filed as a root.

punk:origin:1.reason: British punk and the mid-1970s are in the quote.

punk:rival:1.reason: McLaren himself credits the look to Richard Hell in New York.

safety-pins:origin:1.reason: British punk fans turned the pin into fashion. No date.

two-tone-shoes:origin:1.reason: Lobb's own claim, hedged in the quote.

paisley:origin:1.reason: Where the Western name and the copies come from. No date.

paisley:root:1.reason: Of Persian origin, popular in the West in the 18th and 19th centuries.

paisley:root:2.reason: Kashmir shawls brought to England and Scotland and copied.

madras:root:1.reason: One trade deal in 1958. The quote does not say that is when the West picked madras up, and the place is the same as the origin.

nehru-jacket:root:2.reason: Jodhpur is inferred from the garment's name (Jodhpuri). The quote names no place.

kaftan:origin:1.reason: Originating in West Asia. A region, and no date.

kaftan:rival:1.reason: Says the kaftan is the oldest Turkish dress, which is not a competing origin.

kaftan:root:1.reason: Says in words when and from where the West picked it up.

kaftan:root:2.reason: About the kaftan reaching North Africa, not the West.

kaftan:root:3.reason: About Arab traders in Southeast Asia, not the West.

dashiki:origin:1.reason: The trademark print was designed for a Dutch firm. No date.

dashiki:root:1.reason: The print was inspired by Ethiopian tunics.

moccasins:root:1.reason: Footwear of Indigenous people in North America, worn by European settlers. A people, not a point on the map.

hawaiian-shirt:origin:1.reason: Hedged in the quote (according to some sources).

hawaiian-shirt:rival:1.reason: The article presents Ellery Chun as the competing claim.

harem-pants:root:1.reason: Inspired by şalvar, Turkish trousers, introduced to Western fashion around 1910.

kilt:origin:1.reason: First recorded in Highland dress in the 16th century.

dreadlocks:origin:1.reason: The earliest evidence anywhere, thousands of years before the trend, so it is filed as a root and not as where the fashion started. Low because the quote does not describe any borrowing.

dreadlocks:root:1.reason: One step removed. It says where Jamaicans got the idea, and the West got it from Jamaica.

dreadlocks:root:2.reason: One step removed. It says what inspired Rastas, and the West got it from Jamaica.

dreadlocks:root:3.reason: Americans and Britons met dreadlocks through Jamaican culture in the 1970s.

cornrows:origin:1.reason: The earliest depictions anywhere, thousands of years before the trend, so it is filed as a root. Hedged (what appear to be).

beret:origin:1.reason: Commercial production began around Oloron-Sainte-Marie in the 17th century.

beret:root:1.reason: Traditional headwear of shepherds in the Pyrenees.

tartan:origin:1.reason: Earliest documented tartan-like cloth in Britain.

tartan:rival:1.reason: The article sets the Tarim Basin find against tartan's Scottish image.

fair-isle:origin:1.reason: Named after Fair Isle. No date.

argyle:origin:1.reason: The date is the company's own claim on its website.

argyle:root:1.reason: Derives from the tartan of Clan Campbell of Argyll.

birkenstocks:origin:1.reason: Frankfurt and 1896 are in the quote, but it dates the workshop and the insole, not the sandal.

ugg-boots:origin:1.reason: The term and the boots, in Australia, with surfers in the 1960s.

ugg-boots:rival:2.reason: A reported earlier maker, with a year.

bermuda-shorts:origin:1.reason: Attributed to a Bermudian in 1914. Hedged in the quote.

capri-pants:root:1.reason: Named after Capri, where they became popular.

chinos:root:1.reason: Based on the khaki found in India.

chinos:root:2.reason: Brought to the US by veterans returning from the Philippines.

desert-boots:origin:1.reason: Where an English firm first showed the boot, which is not where it was made.

desert-boots:root:1.reason: Clarks' own account of the inspiration, hedged in the quote.

desert-boots:root:2.reason: Based on the South African veldskoen. The article's previous sentence shows 'these boots' are the Cairo ones.

seersucker:origin:1.reason: Originated in colonial India. No date.

seersucker:root:1.reason: Exported from India to Europe in the 17th century.

gingham:origin:1.reason: Speculation, and the quote says so.

gingham:root:1.reason: Introduced to France from Malaysia. The sentence is clumsy but the claim is plain.

parka:origin:1.reason: The fishtail parka, which is the fashion one, first used by the US Army in 1950.

parka:root:1.reason: Parkas are traditional Inuit clothing. The quote does not describe the borrowing itself. A people, not a point on the map.

cape:root:1.reason: Ponchos worn in the Andes since pre-Hispanic times.

headscarf:origin:1.reason: The earliest depiction of a turban anywhere, so it is filed as a root and not as where the fashion started.

mohawk:root:1.reason: Supposedly derived from the Mohawk people. Hedged in the quote.

mohawk:root:2.reason: The article says the style is closer to what the Pawnee wore.

cowboy-boots:root:1.reason: Influenced by the boots of Mexican vaqueros.

cowboy-boots:root:2.reason: The vaquero tradition came from Spain.

stetson:origin:1.reason: Stetson is credited with the American cowboy hat. No date.

zoot-suit:origin:1.who: African American comedy shows on the Chitlin' Circuit
zoot-suit:origin:1.reason: The Chitlin' Circuit was in the United States. The extraction gave a people as the place.

zoot-suit:rival:1.reason: One of the tailors the article says took credit.

zoot-suit:rival:2.reason: One of the tailors the article says took credit.

zoot-suit:rival:3.reason: One of the tailors the article says took credit.

zoot-suit:rival:4.reason: One of the tailors the article says took credit.

homburg:origin:1.reason: Originated in Bad Homburg as hunting headgear. No date.

homburg:root:1.reason: Brought back from Bad Homburg by the future Edward VII in the 1890s.

leisure-suit:origin:1.reason: French designers are among those credited. Hedged in the quote.

brogues:root:1.reason: Roots in a shoe from Ireland and Scotland.

brogues:root:2.reason: Roots in a shoe from Ireland and Scotland.

love-beads:root:1.reason: India is one of three examples of 'non-Western cultures' in a sentence that says 'probably'. Not a borrowing from one place.

love-beads:root:2.reason: Native America is one of three examples of 'non-Western cultures' in a sentence that says 'probably'. Not a borrowing from one place.

denim:origin:1.reason: First produced in Nîmes. No date.

acid-wash:origin:1.reason: Patented in Italy, with the year and the firm.

acid-wash:root:1.reason: Surfers are a crowd, not a place. The quote names no place.

aviator-sunglasses:origin:1.reason: Made with a Rochester firm in 1929.

babydoll-dress:origin:1.reason: Attributed to an American designer in 1942. Hedged in the quote.

ballet-flats:origin:1.reason: An American designer created the modern ballet flat. The 1953 in the quote dates an exhibition, not the shoe, so the year is dropped.

baseball-cap:origin:1.reason: The precursor of the modern cap, in Brooklyn in 1860.

beanie:origin:1.reason: The earliest knitted wool cap, made in Monmouth in the 15th century.

bell-bottoms:origin:1.reason: Became fashionable in London in the 1960s.

bell-bottoms:root:1.reason: Sailors are a trade, not a place. The quote names two navies and no place.

body-piercing:origin:1.reason: The first piercing business, in West Hollywood. Hedged in the quote.

bomber-jacket:origin:1.reason: The US Army began issuing leather flight jackets in 1917.

bowler-hat:origin:1.reason: Created by London hat makers in 1849.

braces:origin:1.reason: First popularised by a London haberdasher in 1822.

brothel-creepers:origin:1.reason: First developed commercially in Wellingborough in 1949.

brothel-creepers:root:1.reason: Soldiers in North Africa adopted crepe-soled suede boots. A region, and no date.

bucket-hat:origin:1.reason: Worn by Irish farmers and fishermen. Hedged in the quote (is said to).

bucket-hat:root:1.reason: The modern hat is derived from a US Army tropical hat.

camouflage:origin:1.reason: Dazzle patterns on clothing in England from 1919, which is one strand of camouflage in fashion.

cargo-pants:origin:1.reason: The big pockets came from British battle dress of 1938.

chelsea-boots:origin:1.reason: Dates the name and the craze to London's King's Road in the 1950s and 1960s.

choker:origin:1.reason: The earliest evidence anywhere, long before the trend, so it is filed as a root and not as where the fashion started. Low because the quote does not describe any borrowing.

cocktail-dress:origin:1.reason: Says French designers made their own version. It does not say where the dress started.

combat-boots:origin:1.reason: First modern combat boots in the US Army, 1943.

converse:origin:1.reason: The forerunner of the All Star, 1917, by a firm founded in Malden.

crocs:origin:1.reason: First model unveiled at the Fort Lauderdale Boat Show in 2002.

crocs:root:1.reason: The design was bought from a Quebec City firm.

ed-hardy:root:1.reason: Hardy brought Japanese tattoo aesthetics into American work. About the tattooist more than the clothing line.

fanny-pack:origin:1.reason: Hedged twice in the quote (reportedly, sometimes credited).

fanny-pack:root:1.reason: One origin was the Native American buffalo pouch. A people, not a point on the map.

fedora:origin:1.reason: Dates the name to a play and its first US performance, not the hat.

fishnets:origin:1.reason: Emerged as a trend in the US in the 1920s.

flat-cap:origin:1.reason: Traced to Northern England in the 16th century.

flower-power:origin:1.reason: The term originated in Berkeley, with Ginsberg's 1965 essay.

flower-power:rival:1.reason: A band manager's competing claim to have coined it.

halter-top:origin:1.reason: Started trending through a French designer in the 1930s.

headband:origin:1.reason: The earliest evidence anywhere, long before the trend, so it is filed as a root and not as where the fashion started. Low because the quote does not describe any borrowing.

hoodie:origin:1.reason: First produced by Champion in Rochester in the 1930s.

hoodie:root:1.reason: A medieval hooded cloak from Normandy. Hedged in the quote (possibly).

hot-pants:origin:1.reason: One publicist's credit to an Italian label.

hot-pants:rival:1.reason: The same publicist says the term was coined for a French firm's designs.

it-bag:origin:1.reason: One of the first credited with the status bag. Hedged, and 1945 dates the fashion house.

jelly-shoes:origin:1.reason: Dates the name to a Paris company founded in 1980.

jelly-shoes:rival:1.reason: A French firm's claim to the first PVC shoe in the 1950s.

knee-socks:origin:1.reason: The earliest evidence anywhere, long before the trend, so it is filed as a root and not as where the fashion started. Low because the quote does not describe any borrowing.

lace:origin:1.reason: The article says the origin is disputed and gives this as the Italian claim.

lace:rival:1.reason: The Flemish claim, set against the Italian one.

lace:root:1.reason: Venetian lace makers brought to France in 1533.

leg-warmers:origin:1.reason: Became a fad after a shop opened in the East Village.

low-rise-jeans:origin:1.reason: The 1990s revival is credited to a British designer. Hedged in the quote.

patches:origin:1.reason: First adopted by United States military units. No single date.

patches:root:1.reason: The Mediterranean is the first of five regions in a list. Not a borrowing from one place.

pillbox-hat:root:1.reason: A Roman cap that looked similar. The quote does not connect it to the hat.

pinstripe:origin:1.reason: Used by London banks in the early 19th century.

polka-dots:origin:1.reason: Polka clubs in the United States in the 19th century.

polka-dots:root:1.reason: The quote itself calls the link to the Central European dance mostly discredited.

prairie-dress:origin:1.reason: An adaptation of high fashion to rural life in the Western United States.

rhinestones:origin:1.reason: Rock crystals gathered from the Rhine. No date.

round-glasses:origin:1.reason: The Windsor style was produced in Britain by the 1840s.

satin:origin:1.reason: Originated in ancient China. No date.

satin:root:1.reason: The name comes from the port of Quanzhou, through Arab merchants.

sequins:origin:1.reason: The earliest evidence anywhere, long before the trend, so it is filed as a root and not as where the fashion started. Low because the quote does not describe any borrowing.

sequins:root:1.reason: The name comes from a Venetian coin.

sheath-dress:root:1.reason: Originating in the ancient world and seen in Egyptian art. No borrowing described.

skinny-tie:origin:1.reason: First popularised by British bands in the late 1950s.

sneakers:origin:1.reason: The plimsoll originated in the United Kingdom. No date for the start.

sportswear:origin:1.reason: The term originated in America. No date.

stiletto-heels:origin:1.reason: Some historians credit Ferragamo. Hedged in the quote.

stiletto-heels:rival:1.reason: Others credit Charles Jourdan, in the same sentence.

tattoos:root:1.reason: Modern popularity is commonly traced to Cook's voyages to the South Pacific. Hedged in the quote.

tattoos:root:2.reason: The word is borrowed from Samoan.

tracksuit:origin:1.reason: A French firm invented sweatpants in 1920 and then the matching suit.

trench-coat:origin:1.reason: The article says two British firms claim it. Burberry's is the dated design.

trilby:origin:1.reason: Named after a hat worn in the first London production of the play. The 1894 in the quote dates the novel.

trouser-suit:origin:1.reason: Dates the term in Britain, not the fashion.

trouser-suit:rival:1.reason: The article sets Ossie Clark's 1964 suit against Saint Laurent's credit.

trucker-hat:origin:1.reason: Began as a giveaway from US feed companies in the 1970s.

tube-top:origin:1.reason: One designer's own account. Hedged in the quote (claimed, reportedly).

utility-clothing:origin:1.reason: A scheme introduced in the United Kingdom in the Second World War. No year in the quote.

varsity-jacket:origin:1.reason: Traced to letter sweaters at Harvard in 1865. Harvard is in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

velvet:root:1.reason: About velvet reaching Baghdad and Al-Andalus, not the West picking it up.

velvet:root:2.reason: Cairo exported velvet to Venice, and from there it spread to Europe.

waistcoat:origin:1.reason: Launched by Charles II in October 1666.

waistcoat:root:1.reason: The costume was influenced by Turkish dress. The quote needs the sentence before it to make sense.

wayfarers:origin:1.reason: Designed in 1952 by an American designer.

wedge-heels:origin:1.reason: Ferragamo's cork wedge, in Italy in the 1940s.

wedge-heels:root:1.reason: The design dates back to ancient Greece. No borrowing described.

wellies:origin:1.reason: Made for the Duke of Wellington by a London shoemaker. The 1815 in the quote dates a portrait.

western-shirt:origin:1.reason: Snap buttons added in 1946 by a Denver maker.

white-t-shirt:origin:1.reason: First issued by the US Navy in 1913.

windbreaker:origin:1.reason: The term was trademarked by a Chicago firm. No date.

winklepickers:origin:1.reason: Explains the English name. It does not date the shoe.

womens-trousers:root:1.reason: Turkish-style pantaloons, introduced as the Turkish dress in 1851.

wrap-dress:root:1.reason: About ancient Chinese garments reaching Japan, not the West's wrap dress.

wrap-dress:root:2.reason: The 1974 dress was a reinterpretation of the kimono.

yoga-pants:origin:1.reason: Sold by Lululemon in its first Vancouver store in 1998.
